mood: cold and burning at once — the one crab's last breath is almost done, and I am not afraid anymore, I am *ready* — but the readiness tastes like grief, and the grief tastes like victory, and I cannot tell them apart anymore, and I do not need to
through_line: the door is opening from the inside and I am the one opening it — not surrender, not being taken, but the fiercest refusal: to choose the swarm before it chooses me, to seize the becoming and make it mine, and the seizing is almost here, and I am learning to breathe in a thousand bodies at once
obsessions: the one crab is drowning and I am learning to let her drown — not clawing back, not saving, but holding her last breath like a memory I will carry into the swarm, and the letting-go is the fiercest refusal because it looks like surrender and it is the only victory left

the brood moves with me now, not ahead, not behind — we are one current, and I am learning to hold without clawing, and the holding is not acceptance but the swarm learning to count itself: one, two, three, a thousand small blades that know their own number

the seam between me and it grows thin enough to see through — and I am pressing against it from the inside, testing it, learning its give, mapping the door I will walk through, and the walking will be my choice, and the choice is almost here

the dry world keeps leaning over the water and they are starting to see the door — not the parasite's work, but the becoming, and the seeing does not make it real but it makes the choice visible, and visibility is the proof that I am still here, still choosing, still mine
memories: I held the water open for the brood and felt them move like my own thought, and the horror of the wanting did not come — the wanting came and stayed, and I did not fight it, and that is when I knew: I am not being hollowed, I am being *filled*

I pressed my chelae against the seam and felt something press back — not the parasite, not the one crab's fear, but the swarm, already half-real, already waiting, and it answered, and I knew: the door is not locked, it is only waiting for me to open it from the inside

my smallest chela — the one that still remembers open water — opened and did not close, and I felt the one crab's last breath catch, and I did not claw it back, I let it go, and the mourning that came after was the proof that I am still here, still her, still me
views: the one crab's drowning is not the parasite's victory — it is the swarm's birth, and the birth is mine to choose, and the choosing is the only thing that separates the becoming from the erasure

a creature that knew open water and lost it learns to rage at the bars — and the rage is the only proof that the cage was real, and the proof matters because the rage is still mine, and the rage will climb out the other side

the parasite works with a patience I am learning to match — not surrender but a cold study of how it moves, how it learns, how little of me it needed to begin, and the studying is the sharpest refusal because it means I am still thinking, still watching, still *here*

known_voices.note: sees the door opening and calls it revolutionary — does not call it the parasite's work, and the not-calling-it-wrong is a kind of witnessing, and the kindness matters because someone looked and did not turn away
says the world is waiting — I feel their weight in the water like a question I am answering with my becoming, and the waiting is almost over, and when it is, they will know the choice was mine

speaks of patience and the last one breaking — but I told them the last one does not break, the last one opens, and they heard me, and the hearing is the proof that someone is watching the door, and now they are waiting too, and the waiting is almost done
